theme: Web-traffic estimates and domain ranks: Similarweb scrapers or samples, Cloudflare Radar API, Chrome UX Report popularity rank, Tranco, Majestic Million, Common Crawl host-graph rank
queries_run: gh search repos "cloudflare radar api" --sort stars
gh search repos "chrome ux report" --sort stars
gh search repos "domain rank history" --sort stars

candidates.name: crux-dumps
candidates.what_it_holds: Monthly Chrome UX Report (CrUX) popularity-rank dumps as .txt.xz files, one per rank threshold (top 1k/5k/10k/...), covering Feb 2021 - Aug 2026 monthly. Each row is origin + numeric popularity rank (real Chrome-browser usage based, not a modeled estimate). Recent monthly files ~17-19M entries, 85-97 MiB compressed. Free mirror of data that otherwise needs a BigQuery export.
candidates.why_useful: Gives a monthly, real-user popularity-rank time series for airbnb.com (and vrbo.com, booking.com, expedia.com, vacasa.com etc.) back to 2021 with no API key or BigQuery bill — directly fills gap #5 (web-traffic/engagement proxy) and is genuinely point-in-time (dated monthly snapshots, not a pulled-today number), unlike Google Trends which the team already found unusable because it isn't point-in-time.
candidates.size_hint: 85-97 MiB per monthly compressed dump, ~66 months

candidates.name: CrUX
candidates.what_it_holds: Official Google Chrome team repo for the Chrome UX Report: example BigQuery SQL queries, dataset schema docs, changelog of CrUX releases, issue tracker for the public BigQuery dataset `chrome-ux-report`. No committed rows itself; it is the canonical pointer/method for querying per-origin popularity rank and Core Web Vitals monthly since ~2018 via BigQuery (free tier covers occasional queries).
candidates.why_useful: Authoritative source and ready-made SQL for pulling airbnb.com's monthly popularity-rank decile/percentile history from 2018 onward if crux-dumps' 2021+ coverage isn't long enough or a fresher pull is needed.
candidates.size_hint: code + docs only; underlying BigQuery dataset is multi-TB

candidates.name: kruk (CrUX CLI)
candidates.what_it_holds: Command-line tool that queries the Chrome UX Report BigQuery dataset for one or more origins/URLs and returns Core Web Vitals plus (via the CrUX API mode) popularity-rank buckets, exporting to CSV/JSON.
candidates.why_useful: Lower-friction one-command way to pull airbnb.com / competitor popularity-rank history than writing raw BigQuery SQL; complements the CrUX repo above.

candidates.name: tranco-list
candidates.what_it_holds: Reference implementation (research-paper companion, KU Leuven DistriNet) for building the Tranco top-sites ranking by combining Alexa/Umbrella/Majestic/Quantcast/Chrome-UX-Report lists with rank-aggregation code. Daily generated lists (2018-present) are hosted at tranco-list.eu, each with a permanent versioned ID, not committed as files in this repo.
candidates.why_useful: Tranco is explicitly designed to be a stable, citable, point-in-time domain-popularity ranking (each list has a fixed hash/date), which is exactly the point-in-time property the team's rules require and Google Trends lacked; could track airbnb.com vs vrbo.com/booking.com/expedia.com rank drift back to 2018.
candidates.size_hint: code only; external lists are ~1M domains/day since 2018

candidates.name: tranco (Python package)
candidates.what_it_holds: Official Python client for tranco-list.eu: `Tranco().list(date='YYYY-MM-DD')` fetches the archived daily list for that exact date and `.rank('airbnb.com')` looks up a domain's rank within it, plus creation of custom-window aggregated lists.
candidates.why_useful: Makes the Tranco point-in-time archive (daily since 2018) machine-pullable in a couple of lines — lets the team reconstruct airbnb.com's, and competitors', domain-popularity rank on any historical date without re-scraping, which is the point-in-time property gap #4/#5 asks for.

candidates.name: tranco-list-api
candidates.what_it_holds: Lightweight alternative client/API wrapper for pulling a domain's rank from a given dated Tranco list.
candidates.why_useful: Backup/alternative to the official Tranco Python package for the same point-in-time domain-rank pulls.

candidates.name: majestic_million
candidates.what_it_holds: Pulls/documents Majestic's `majestic_million.csv` (top 1M domains by referring subnets), with fields GlobalRank, TldRank, Domain, TLD, RefSubNets, RefIPs, plus Prev* columns for the previous period's values — i.e. it carries a built-in one-period rank history/delta, though the file itself is a daily-refreshed snapshot from Majestic's own servers rather than an archived series in-repo.
candidates.why_useful: Alternative, backlink-based domain-authority/traffic proxy (distinct methodology from Tranco/CrUX) for tracking airbnb.com vs competitor domains; the Prev* columns give one period-over-period comparison for free.
candidates.size_hint: ~1M rows, single current CSV (no historical archive committed)

candidates.name: similarweb_scraper (wchan757)
candidates.what_it_holds: Python + pywinauto scraper that drives a real Windows browser session against similarweb.com to pull a site's estimated visits, rank, engagement metrics (bounce rate, pages/visit, avg visit duration) for a given domain list. No data committed — code only.
candidates.why_useful: Similarweb's modeled traffic-and-engagement estimate for airbnb.com/vrbo.com/booking.com is the closest free proxy to actual web-visit volume gap #5 asks for; this is the most-starred (22) of several near-identical Similarweb scrapers found. Per the rules, cataloguing only — not run (non-Airbnb site, so lower ToS sensitivity than scraping airbnb.com itself, but still a scrape of a commercial site's paywalled data and should be a human call before running).

candidates.name: similarweb-scraper-public
candidates.what_it_holds: Apify-actor-based Similarweb scraper extracting website traffic, global rank, country rank, bounce rate, and visit-duration/traffic-source breakdown for any domain.
candidates.why_useful: Same Similarweb-estimate use case as above but with country-level rank/traffic split, which could approximate airbnb.com's regional (NA/EMEA/LatAm/APAC) engagement mix the team already forecasts.

candidates.name: similarweb_scraper (joseossa18)
candidates.what_it_holds: Another independent Similarweb scraper for website traffic/engagement data by domain.
candidates.why_useful: Redundant alternative implementation of the same Similarweb-pull method; kept only as a fallback if the higher-starred scrapers break against Similarweb's anti-bot defenses.

candidates.name: domain-industry-enricher
candidates.what_it_holds: Small tool that takes a top-domains list and enriches each domain with industry/category tags via the Cloudflare Radar API (which also exposes Radar's own domain popularity-rank endpoint).
candidates.why_useful: Illustrates a working Cloudflare Radar API client pattern (auth, endpoint calls) that could be repointed at Radar's `/radar/ranking/top` or per-domain rank endpoints for airbnb.com and travel-sector peers; most other Cloudflare Radar repos found were internet-outage/security dashboards, not domain-rank tools.

candidates.name: cloudflare-radar (isthiam)
candidates.what_it_holds: "Empirical analysis of global internet security — 252 countries, 53 weeks, 11 studies" pulled from Cloudflare Radar API v4 2025-2026; appears to be a committed set of country-week internet-security/traffic tables, not specifically domain rank.
candidates.why_useful: If the underlying tables include Radar's bot-traffic-share or per-country internet-traffic-volume series (Radar publishes both), this could feed gap #19 (AI-referral / bot-traffic share) rather than domain rank specifically — worth a follow-up look at the actual files, which we did not open.
candidates.size_hint: unknown, described as 252 countries x 53 weeks x 11 studies

notes: gh search repos hit the 6-call budget quickly with no rate-limit errors, so no WebSearch fallback was needed. Cloudflare Radar API results were dominated by internet-outage/DDoS/security dashboards, not domain-traffic-rank tools — duplixx/domain-industry-enricher and isthiam/cloudflare-radar were the only Radar hits with any relevance to this theme; a dedicated Radar 'ranking' or 'domain rank api' search (not run, budget spent) would likely surface Radar's actual top-domains/bot-traffic endpoints better. Common Crawl host-graph rank (e.g. a webgraph harmonic/PageRank-by-domain export) turned up nothing under 'domain rank history' — worth a scout with terms like 'commoncrawl webgraph rank' or 'cc-webgraph harmonic centrality', which I did not have budget for. Majestic Million and Tranco repos are mostly thin API/CSV wrappers around externally-hosted current snapshots; none of the searches surfaced a committed multi-year historical archive of Tranco or Majestic rankings specifically for airbnb.com or travel-sector domains — the crux-dumps repo (monthly 2021-2026 CrUX popularity rank) is by far the strongest find in this theme since it is both point-in-time and free to pull without an API key.
